mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team B's shots-for is above competition average but shots-on-target-for is below competition average (i.e. low conversion ratio), AND Team A's shots-on-target-against recent-5 is below its all-prior average. Both conditions must hold simultaneously.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's shots-to-shots-on-target conversion ratio is low AND Team A's recent shots-on-target-against is suppressed relative to season average, Team B's effective attacking output (shots-on-target-for) is further suppressed relative to its raw shot volume.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shot volume is high but its conversion to shots-on-target is disproportionately low, and this gap between total shots and shots-on-target has widened further in recent matches; jointly, Team A's defensive shots-on-target allowed has improved in recent matches relative to its season average. The joint relationship between Team B's shots-for vs shots-on-target ratio and Team A's shots-on-target-against ratio conditions the expected quality of Team B's attacking threat beyond what either observable alone captures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint relationship across two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) for two different teams simultaneously, and compares a ratio (shots vs shots-on-target) against a cross-team defensive suppression signal. It cannot be reduced to a single observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team B's shots-against (all-prior and recent-5) is substantially above competition average, while Team A's shots-for (all-prior and recent-5) is near or below competition average. The asymmetry between Team B's defensive exposure and Team A's offensive output is the conditioning structure.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's shots-against is elevated above competition average and Team A's shots-for is near competition average, Team A's shots-on-target-for is expected to rise relative to its own baseline, because the opponent's defensive exposure amplifies even modest attacking volume.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B concedes a high volume of shots (well above competition average, and rising sharply in recent matches), while Team A produces shots at a level close to competition average but with a stable shots-on-target rate. The asymmetric relationship — Team B allows many shots while Team A's shot production is modest but consistent — jointly determines the expected shots-on-target volume for Team A in this fixture, in a way that differs from reading either team's observable in isolation.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross-team relationship between two different observables (Team A shots-for vs Team B shots-against), not a same-observable mirror. It requires jointly conditioning on both teams' values and comparing them to a competition baseline, which is structurally richer than any single-observable split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team B's fouls-for recent-5 is elevated above its season average AND above competition average, while Team A's corner-kicks-against recent-5 is below its season average. Measure whether this joint state predicts elevated second-half cards (cards_2h) relative to competition baseline.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's recent foul rate is elevated and Team A's corner-kicks-against is suppressed, second-half card volume rises above competition average, because foul-prone teams under defensive pressure generate more disciplinary events in the second half.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's foul rate has surged in recent matches (recent-5 well above its season average and above competition average), while Team A's corner-kicks-against has improved (recent-5 below season average). The joint relationship between Team B's recent foul elevation and Team A's corner-kick-against suppression conditions the expected second-half card volume, since elevated fouls in a team that already concedes corners at a high rate historically co-occur with increased second-half card accumulation.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a genuine joint relationship across three distinct observables (fouls, corner_kicks, cards_2h) and requires conditioning on two different team-level signals simultaneously — not reducible to any single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team B's offsides-for recent-5 is substantially above its season average, AND Team A's offsides-against recent-5 is below its season average. Within this joint state, examine whether Team B's possession and corner-kick production are suppressed relative to their season averages.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's recent offside rate is elevated and Team A's offside-against rate is suppressed, Team B's effective possession and corner-kick production are further reduced, because high offside frequency reflects a high defensive line that disrupts Team B's attacking structure.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's offsides-for has surged sharply in recent matches (recent-5 nearly double its season average), while Team A's offsides-against has declined in recent matches. The joint divergence between Team B's recent offside rate and Team A's recent offside-against rate — both moving in opposite directions from their season averages — signals a structural mismatch in attacking line management that conditions corner-kick and possession outcomes.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (offsides-for and offsides-against) for two different teams, and then examining a third observable (possession/corners) as the outcome. The two-team, two-observable conditioning structure is not reducible to any single-observable split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint within-match state: both teams show higher goal rates in the second half than the first half (half-level split), AND Team A's recent defensive form is sharply improved while Team B's is not. Measure whether the second-half goal rate is disproportionately elevated relative to the first half when both teams share this back-loaded pattern and defensive form diverges.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams individually show a back-loaded goal pattern (second-half rate exceeds first-half rate) and Team A's recent defensive form is improved while Team B's is not, the second half is expected to concentrate a disproportionate share of total match goals relative to competition average half-distribution.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's goals-for first-half rate is substantially below its second-half rate (0.492 vs 0.785 per match), while Team B's goals-against first-half rate is also below its second-half rate (0.797 vs 0.984). The joint within-match half-level asymmetry — both teams showing a back-loaded goal pattern — conditions the expected half-by-half goal distribution in a way that is not captured by full-match goal averages alone. Additionally, Team A's recent goals-against has dropped sharply (recent-5: 0.4 vs season: 1.554), while Team B's recent goals-against remains elevated (recent-5: 1.8 vs season: 1.781), creating a cross-team asymmetry in defensive form that further conditions the half-level goal distribution.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a within-match half-level split (first half vs second half goals) jointly conditioned on both teams' half-level patterns simultaneously, plus a cross-team asymmetry in recent defensive form. It is not reducible to a single observable with one band — it requires half-resolution data and a two-team joint conditioning structure.
